three-nested.why: Three nested loops, each running n times: n × n × n.

sqrt-loop.why: The loop stops once i² passes n, so it runs about √n times: slower-growing than n, faster than log n.

halving-inner.why: The inner loop halves j, so it runs about log₂ n times for each of the n outer iterations.

rows-and-columns.why: Every cell is visited once. r and c are independent, so neither can be replaced by the other.

shrinking-window.why: left only moves forward, at most n times in total, and each map operation is O(1) on average.

halving-recursion.why: One call per halving: about log₂ n calls, each doing constant work.

linear-recursion-space.why: The calls nest n deep before any returns, so n frames are on the stack at once.

permutations.why: There are n! orderings, so producing them is at least n! work: an output-sensitive bound.

copy-then-scan.why: The copy is n extra ints, however fast the rest of the method is.
